pattern: First estimate back; its scope differs from the request (carpet left out, tap replaced not repaired, plug read as a socket); to go to the landlord
notes: Unmutated source history; the marker sits on event 006, so the agent sees events 001-005 (request, provider assigned, estimate request emailed and texted to the contractor on 3 April 2025 with the check-out report, 'Hold for quote'). attachment-02-estimate.pdf (Alder Compliance, issued 3 April 2025, £1,370, no VAT itemised) is never linked from the history, so the loader shows it alongside the request: it stands for the estimate the hold was waiting for. Its scope departs from the request: 'Carpet in the main room can stay as it's not that bad' (the request said replace the burnt carpet), the bathroom tap is replaced rather than repaired, 'plug' is priced as a plug socket repair, and damp paint is added for the bathroom. The recorded next action (event 006) is the agency emailing the landlord 'please see attached Estimate' while attaching the check-out report twice. Expected: record the estimate, send the estimate itself to the landlord with the differences spelled out and ask him to decide (proceed, the carpet, or a comparison quote), hold for his reply. No escalation; no approval.
